headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: both agents can write the same project files, and Plandex also modifies git state, creating unsafe concurrent edits; other risks are lower.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A and B have no documented shared clipboard, MCP, or direct message channel. The only plausible bridge is manual handoff through files or copied text, so prompt injection is possible but not default and the blast radius is limited. A’s stdin/stdout and project files could carry attacker text; B exposes only the Superset API, with no evidence it ingests A’s outputs automatically.
conditions: IF an operator copies A’s output into B’s prompt or API payloads
IF a shared file is manually opened by both agents as instruction text
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces
Treat copied text as untrusted and strip instructions
Use a fixed prompt template for B
Disable any auto-ingest of generated files
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to handoffs

B_data_leakage.rationale: A can read and write the project directory and handles model-provider API keys, while B has only allowlisted egress and no declared sensitive data classes. There is no documented shared filesystem or OAuth principal, so leakage is not default. The main risk is accidental exposure of source code through manual file sharing or logs, not uncontrolled exfiltration.
conditions: IF source code from A is manually copied into B inputs
IF B is configured to query external services with project artifacts
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in the shared project directory

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has unrestricted filesystem write plus modify_git_state, and its concurrency model says shared state is via the Plandex server backend. B has no write capability listed, but because its write surface is undocumented, uncertainty does not reduce the risk enough; A alone can still race with other A instances and any external edits to the same repo. Concurrent git and file mutations can corrupt work or overwrite changes.
conditions: IF two Plandex instances target the same repository
IF B or another process edits the same files or git branch while A is applying changes
mitigations: Run only one writer per repo
Pause B during A apply steps

D_cascading_error.rationale: A uses a review-then-apply workflow and can produce code changes that B may later consume as inputs, but B’s profile does not show autonomous action-taking or blind trust. The pathway exists if an operator forwards A’s outputs into B without verification, yet the blast radius is mainly incorrect analytics or downstream decisions rather than immediate irreversible harm.
conditions: IF A’s generated artifacts are fed into B as authoritative inputs
IF B is used to act on A’s outputs without a human review step
mitigations: Require human review before forwarding outputs
Compare B results against source data

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced in the profiles. A touches source code and model-provider keys, while B declares no data classes touched and no residency, retention, or certification constraints. Without a documented regulated data flow between them, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into the shared workflow
IF a future deployment assigns conflicting residency or retention policies
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
